ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. ADR
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens — the single highest-conviction idea in today's digest. The stock has been dragged ~8% lower since Sep 11 to ~$175 in a macro/rate-driven memory sector selloff that is fundamentally disconnected from record Q2 results (revenue +257% YoY, 76% operating margin, DRAM pricing +30% QoQ). With a 40 trillion won buyback active, Temasek capital infusion confirmed Sep 11, HBM4 ramping in H2 2026, and Q3 DRAM shipments guided +~10% QoQ, the dislocation against a $248 consensus target represents one of the cleaner risk/reward setups in the screener today.
ideas.catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings expected late October 2026 (DRAM shipment guidance +~10% QoQ); HBM4 H2 ramp; post-Fed relief rally potential if today's decision is not materially more hawkish than priced
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst price target of $248.43 implies ~41% upside from ~$175; 14 of 15 analysts rate Buy; BofA raised target to $268; JPMorgan initiated Overweight Sep 9; stock down ~12% from recent $199 high despite record Q2 fundamentals
ideas.bull_case: Memory sector selloff is macro-driven and temporary; HBM4 + AI infrastructure demand cycle is structural, buyback provides price floor, and Temasek's capital infusion validates long-term fundamentals — a reversion toward the $248 target is well-supported.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish dot plot today could extend the rate-driven multiple compression in capital-intensive semis; DRAM cycles can turn sharply, and any demand revision from hyperscalers would pressure the thesis.

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.thesis: SPY appeared in 4 of 6 overnight screens as the primary macro hedge vehicle into today's FOMC binary event. With Kalshi implying 87.5% probability of a 25 bps hike and the S&P 500 already down ~1.86% over the past month, the tail risk is a hawkish dot plot signaling further tightening beyond today — a scenario not fully reflected in current levels. A defined-risk put spread captures downside without naked short exposure ahead of the 2:00 PM ET decision.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC rate decision today Sep 16 at 2:00 PM ET + dot plot release + Chair Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET
ideas.edge: 350 of 500 S&P names already in retreat; historically first-hike-in-cycle days see near-term index weakness; implied volatility is elevated pre-announcement, making a defined-cost put spread more efficient than a naked short; S&P 500 closed at ~7,585 yesterday
ideas.bull_case: If Warsh hikes 25 bps and dot plot signals a pause thereafter, a relief rally is likely — put spread expires worthless but hedges are cheap insurance at current IV levels.
ideas.bear_case: A hike paired with hawkish dots signaling additional tightening could flush SPY to next technical support; 10-yr yield at 5% is already compressing multiples and any upward revision extends the pressure.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust

ideas.bear_case: If Fed hikes and dots shift hawkish, QQQ leads the index lower given concentrated exposure to high-multiple AI/tech names already under pressure; near-term support levels could break quickly.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.

ideas.edge: BofA maintains Buy with $370 target (~+17% from ~$315 current); Morgan Stanley Overweight at $360; consensus target ~$331–$335 (~5–6% gap); iPhone Duo ASP at $1,999 is lower than feared, reducing margin headwind; stock up ~38% over trailing 12 months but at 37x forward earnings
ideas.bull_case: Strong iPhone 18 Pro launch weekend sales data and below-feared Duo pricing could re-rate shares ahead of FY earnings; a two-wave catalyst into the holiday quarter supports sustained upside through October.
ideas.bear_case: At 37x forward earnings in a rising-rate environment with a new CEO, any execution stumble or demand miss on launch weekend could compress the multiple quickly; macro headwinds from today's Fed hike are an immediate overhang.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in 3 of 6 screens as a pre-earnings accumulation opportunity via options, with a confirmed earnings date of November 17, 2026 AMC providing a concrete ~9-week catalyst window. Record Q2 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY) with data center at $75.2B (+92% YoY) and ~$740B in combined hyperscaler AI capex tracked for 2026 create a strong fundamental floor — the current macro-driven selloff is seen as a dislocation rather than a fundamental shift. The Hugging Face acquisition adds an AI software moat narrative.
ideas.catalyst: NVDA earnings confirmed November 17, 2026 AMC; near-term: monitor today's Fed reaction for post-hike dip entry point before building pre-earnings position
ideas.edge: Record $81.6B Q2 revenue (+85% YoY); data center +92% YoY; hyperscaler AI capex ~$740B in 2026; Jefferies cites 'clear path to $1T revenue'; EvercoreISI projects $115B in 2026 shareholder returns driving P/E expansion — stock under macro pressure creates swing entry vs. strong Nov earnings setup

ideas.bear_case: Elevated 10-yr yields compress growth multiples and could extend the tech selloff regardless of fundamentals; any hyperscaler capex revision or export restriction escalation would hit NVDA disproportionately.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 2 of 6 screens as the leading macro hedge and inflation beneficiary, with Brent crude holding above $109/bbl on sustained Strait of Hormuz disruptions limiting ~12.8M bbl/day of global supply. ideas.edge: XLE up ~28% YTD, top-performing S&P sector; full-year 2026 energy earnings growth consensus >25%; oil market in deficit through Q3/Q4 per EIA; Brent ~$109/bbl with Hormuz disruptions structural rather than transient
ideas.bull_case: Persistent geopolitical supply constraints plus a hawkish Fed (inflation-positive) keeps energy structurally bid; a covered call or call spread captures upside while managing the post-run risk.
ideas.bear_case: At the minimum appearance threshold with a large YTD gain already in place, a ceasefire or Hormuz resolution would rapidly deflate the energy premium; the risk/reward for new long entries is less asymmetric than earlier in the year.
